Purpose: Provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem.

Visual:
    Client ──► Facade ──┬──► SubsystemA
                        ├──► SubsystemB
                        ├──► SubsystemC
                        └──► SubsystemD

    Instead of:
    Client ──┬──► SubsystemA
             ├──► SubsystemB
             ├──► SubsystemC
             └──► SubsystemD

Real Example - Home Theater System:
    Turn on TV + Set input + Start sound system + Dim lights
    = Just call: homeTheater.watchMovie()

Use Cases:
- Simplifying complex libraries
- Providing easy-to-use interface
- Reducing dependencies

```python
class UnderlineDecorator(TextDecorator):
    def render(self) -> str:
        return f"__{self._component.render()}__"

# Create formatted text
text = PlainText("Hello World")
print(f"Plain: {text.render()}")

bold_text = BoldDecorator(PlainText("Hello World"))
print(f"Bold: {bold_text.render()}")

italic_bold = ItalicDecorator(BoldDecorator(PlainText("Hello World")))
print(f"Bold + Italic: {italic_bold.render()}")

full_format = UnderlineDecorator(ItalicDecorator(BoldDecorator(PlainText("Hello World"))))
print(f"Bold + Italic + Underline: {full_format.render()}")
```

Purpose: Provide a placeholder/surrogate for another object to control access.

Visual:
    Client ──► Proxy ──► RealSubject

    Types of Proxies:
    1. Virtual Proxy - Lazy initialization
    2. Protection Proxy - Access control
    3. Remote Proxy - Remote object representation
    4. Caching Proxy - Cache results

Use Cases:
- Lazy loading of expensive objects
- Access control and security
- Caching and memoization
- Logging and monitoring

```python
# Facade
class HomeTheaterFacade:
    def __init__(self):
        self.tv = TV()
        self.sound = SoundSystem()
        self.dvd = DVDPlayer()
        self.lights = Lights()
    
    def watch_movie(self, movie):
        print("\n🍿 Setting up movie night...")
        self.lights.dim(10)
        self.tv.on()
        self.tv.set_input("DVD")
        self.sound.on()
        self.sound.set_volume(30)
        self.dvd.on()
        self.dvd.play(movie)
        print("🎬 Enjoy your movie!\n")
    
    def end_movie(self):
        print("\n🛑 Shutting down...")
        self.dvd.off()
        self.sound.off()
        self.tv.off()
        self.lights.on()
        print("✅ All done!\n")

theater = HomeTheaterFacade()
theater.watch_movie("The Matrix")
theater.end_movie()

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. PROXY PATTERN
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

sections.body:
Protection proxy with access control

```python
class BankAccountProxy(BankAccount):
    """Protection proxy with access control"""
    def __init__(self, balance, user_role):
        self._real_account = RealBankAccount(balance)
        self.user_role = user_role
    
    def withdraw(self, amount):
        if self.user_role != "owner":
            return "🚫 Access denied! Only owner can withdraw"
        return self._real_account.withdraw(amount)
    
    def deposit(self, amount):
        # Anyone can deposit
        return self._real_account.deposit(amount)
    
    def get_balance(self):
        if self.user_role not in ["owner", "admin"]:
            return "🚫 Access denied! Cannot view balance"
        return self._real_account.get_balance()

# Test protection proxy
print("\n👤 User with 'owner' role:")
owner_account = BankAccountProxy(1000, "owner")
print(owner_account.get_balance())
print(owner_account.withdraw(100))
print(owner_account.deposit(50))

print("\n🚫 User with 'guest' role:")
guest_account = BankAccountProxy(1000, "guest")
print(guest_account.get_balance())
print(guest_account.withdraw(100))
print(guest_account.deposit(50))
```

```python
class LogObserver(Observer):
    def update(self, subject):
        print(f"   📝 LogObserver: Logging event '{subject.get_state()}'")

# Demo
print("\n🔍 Testing Observer Pattern:")
subject = Subject()

# Create observers
email_obs = EmailObserver()
sms_obs = SMSObserver()
log_obs = LogObserver()

# Attach observers
print("\n1. Attaching observers:")
subject.attach(email_obs)
subject.attach(sms_obs)
subject.attach(log_obs)

# Change state - all observers notified
subject.set_state("New product launched!")
subject.set_state("50% OFF Sale!")

# Detach one observer
print("\n2. Detaching SMS observer:")
subject.detach(sms_obs)

subject.set_state("System maintenance tonight")

# Real-world example: Stock market
print("\n\n📈 Another Example - Stock Market:")

class Stock(Subject):
    def __init__(self, symbol, price):
        super().__init__()
        self.symbol = symbol
        self._price = price
    
    def set_price(self, price):
        print(f"\n💹 {self.symbol} price changed: ${self._price} → ${price}")
        self._price = price
        self.notify()
    
    def get_price(self):
        return self._price
```

Purpose: Define family of algorithms, encapsulate each one, and make them interchangeable.

Visual:
    Context ──uses──► Strategy (Interface)
                            ▲
                            │
          ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
          │                 │                 │
    StrategyA          StrategyB          StrategyC

Real Example - Payment Methods:
    Shopping Cart ──► Payment Strategy
                      ├── Credit Card
                      ├── PayPal
                      └── Bitcoin

Use Cases:
- Multiple algorithms for same task
- Sorting strategies
- Compression algorithms
- Payment methods

```python
class InvestorObserver(Observer):
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
    
    def update(self, stock):
        price = stock.get_price()
        print(f"   👤 {self.name}: {stock.symbol} is now ${price}")

# Create stock and investors
apple_stock = Stock("AAPL", 150.00)

investor1 = InvestorObserver("Alice")
investor2 = InvestorObserver("Bob")
investor3 = InvestorObserver("Charlie")

apple_stock.attach(investor1)
apple_stock.attach(investor2)
apple_stock.attach(investor3)

# Price changes notify all investors
apple_stock.set_price(155.00)
apple_stock.set_price(148.50)
```

```python
# Context
class ShoppingCart:
    def __init__(self):
        self.items = []
        self.payment_strategy = None
    
    def add_item(self, item, price):
        self.items.append((item, price))
        print(f"   🛒 Added: {item} (${price})")
    
    def set_payment_strategy(self, strategy: PaymentStrategy):
        self.payment_strategy = strategy
    
    def checkout(self):
        total = sum(price for _, price in self.items)
        print(f"\n💰 Total: ${total}")
        if self.payment_strategy:
            result = self.payment_strategy.pay(total)
            print(f"   {result}")
            print("   ✅ Order completed!")
        else:
            print("   ❌ No payment method set!")
        return total

# Demo
print("\n🔍 Testing Strategy Pattern:")

print("\n1. Shopping with Credit Card:")
cart1 = ShoppingCart()
cart1.add_item("Laptop", 999)
cart1.add_item("Mouse", 25)
cart1.set_payment_strategy(CreditCardStrategy("1234-5678-9012-3456"))
cart1.checkout()

print("\n2. Shopping with PayPal:")
cart2 = ShoppingCart()
cart2.add_item("Book", 29)
cart2.add_item("Pen", 5)
cart2.set_payment_strategy(PayPalStrategy("user@example.com"))
cart2.checkout()

print("\n3. Shopping with Bitcoin:")
cart3 = ShoppingCart()
cart3.add_item("Coffee", 5)
cart3.set_payment_strategy(BitcoinStrategy("1A1zP1eP5QGefi2DMPTfTL5SLmv7DivfNa"))
cart3.checkout()

print("\n\n🔢 Another Example - Sorting Strategies:")

class SortStrategy(ABC):

    def sort(self, data):
        pass
```
